correctness.rationale: Universal m≤2n result: for each player at first turn, any then-available singleton can be secured by unilateral deviation; with monotonicity equilibrium payoff dominates its singleton value. Any opposing bundle has at most two goods, at most one preceding that first turn; deleting one good reduces it to an available singleton or empty bundle, proving EF1. For three players and seven goods, the exact SPNE recurrence is necessary/sufficient by off-path minimum-payoff continuation induction. The checker recomputes all 128 states twice, confirms two root allocations, constructs a 13,700-node SPNE strategy tree, and certifies the B-to-A gap 1092<1161. Strict subset preferences follow from binary perturbations with 128 multiple base.

originality.rationale: Primary §4 of Goldberg–Hollender–Tyrovolas (arXiv:2609.18309v1) provides an online nine-good unique-unfair-SPNE example, not existential seven-good minimality or the general monotone two-round safe region. Amanatidis et al. (arXiv:2610.23686v1) provide a distinct eight-good *offline reporting PNE* counterexample; that is not the online extensive-form SPNE model. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches found no stronger covering implication. An unindexed equivalent statement remains a real priority risk.
residual_risks: A prior seven-good online SPNE counterexample or an equivalent n-agent two-round EF1 theorem could exist outside accessible/indexed literature.
There are two SPNE outcomes in the seven-good witness, one EF1 and one non-EF1; unlike the prior nine-good example, failure is not unavoidable.

value.rationale: This settles the exact first possible existential EF1 failure horizon for three-agent online strategic round-robin, improving the known nine-good online witness to seven while proving robust safety for all normalized monotone valuations through two full rounds for any number of agents. The exact, strict-positive witness and complete SPNE calculation reveal how the third draft round creates the fairness failure, a nonroutine structural boundary.
